key_insight: PanoGS-SLAM extends 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM to panoramic cameras, improving pose stability and mapping quality when the robot moves quickly or changes viewpoint dramatically. The wider field of view gives stronger geometric and photometric constraints than narrow-FoV camera setups.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the instability of real-time dense SLAM methods based on 3D Gaussian Splatting when using narrow-FoV pinhole cameras, especially under fast motion, large viewpoint changes, and dynamic or fast-changing environments.
method: Uses panoramic camera input to capture much more scene context than standard pinhole-based SLAM systems.
Adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting for real-time dense mapping and pose estimation in a panoramic setting.
Improves pose observability and stabilizes photometric optimization during rapid motion and challenging viewpoint transitions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in robotics and AR/VR, this work suggests a more robust SLAM design for environments where standard cameras struggle. It can enable denser, more stable mapping and localization in real-world scenarios with fast motion or wide-area coverage needs.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of narrow-FoV vs panoramic camera coverage

Trajectory plot highlighting improved pose stability under fast motion
Rendered map or point-cloud/Gaussian visualization of the reconstructed scene
paper_authors: Yongqi Mao, Hao Shi, Yufan Zhang, Zhonghua Yi, Xiangfei Guo
